headline: New York Rangers react to Igor Shesterkin's season-ending injury: 'Horrible to hear'
take:
The Athletic reports that New York Rangers goalie Igor Shesterkin will miss the rest of the season with a lower-body injury, with the team reacting to the news as "horrible to hear."

The numbers show how much this costs. Shesterkin has saved 4.88 goals above expected in just 5 games so far this season, on a .927 save percentage, after saving 21.47 goals above expected over 51 games last season. Elite goaltending of that kind is what has kept NYR at 6-3-0 (12 points in 9 games). The team has been only slightly ahead on chance quality, with a 53.3% share of expected goals overall and exactly 50% at five-on-five, so the skaters have not been driving the results alone. The team has also scored 0.9 fewer goals than its expected total, which means the margin has come from the crease. NYR as a whole sits at 4.3 goals saved above expected, and Shesterkin accounts for most of that. Without him, an even five-on-five team loses its safety net, and the penalty kill (0.41 expected goals allowed per game) leans on goaltending too. For fantasy managers, his value goes to zero for the year, and the Rangers' backup becomes a much bigger piece of their outlook.
